First, we complete the square for the expression inside the square root:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-8x+15 & ={x}^{2}-2\cdot 4x+({4}^{2}-{4}^{2})+15 \\  & =({x}^{2}-2\cdot 4x+{4}^{2})-16+15 \\  & =(x-4)^{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given integral, we get

$$
{\int }_{4+\sqrt{2}}^{6}\frac{12}{|x-4|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-8x+15}}\,\text{d}x=12{\int }_{4+\sqrt{2}}^{6}\frac{1}{|x-4|\sqrt{(x-4)^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This resembles the basic integral for inverse secant:

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u=\text{arcsec}\,u+C
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $(x-4).$

So, let's perform the substitution

$$
u=x-4.
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

Let's use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u.$

| $x$ | $4+\sqrt{2}$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\sqrt{2}$ | $2$ |

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4+\sqrt{2}}^{6}\frac{12}{|x-4|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-8x+15}}\,\text{d}x & =12{\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{2}\frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =12\,\text{arcsec}\,u\,{|}_{\sqrt{2}}^{2} \\  & =12(\text{arcsec}(2)-\text{arcsec}(\sqrt{2})) \\  & =12(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
